chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Fadala and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), how much the prayer in it is equivalent to? He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: A prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except for the Sacred Mosque.'

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (Prophet's Mosque in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for praying in the Prophet's Mosque compared to other mosques?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent Tusi companions Safwan, Fadal, and Ibn Abi Umayr, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the unique spiritual status of Al-Masjid Al-Nabawi as the second holiest site in Islam. It clarifies the hierarchy of reward by distinguishing the Prophet's Mosque from Al-Masjid Al-Haram, which retains its singular preeminence, while affirming the specific merit of Medina's sanctity in Shia jurisprudence.
